name: Dalton Omondi Opondo
engineeringObjective: Electrical & Electronics Engineering student at Kenyatta University building AI assessment infrastructure, embedded hardware systems, and scalable education technologies across Africa.
researchStatement: AI engineer & Olympiad trainer investigating neural architecture co-design, reasoning benchmarks (ARC Prize, AIMO), structured sparsity (ZPSN), and silicon photonics for next-generation intelligent systems.
bio: Building intelligent systems at the intersection of AI, embedded engineering, and education. Founder of Proctor AI, IEEEXtreme 18.0 Rank #1 team in Kenya, IEEE Tech Ignite 1st Runner-Up, International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) participant, and Chief Trainer for the Kenya Mathematical Olympiad.

about.approach: Where software intelligence meets physical reality — that's where I build. My work is driven by a simple core idea: building functional systems over performing. Whether I'm training a computer vision model, architecting a backend API, laying out a circuit board, or prototyping an embedded node, I bring the same focus to technical precision and real-world utility. I believe the most compelling work happens when you bridge disciplines — bringing the rigor of hardware engineering to AI systems, and the adaptability of machine learning to physical devices.
about.lookingFor: Currently scaling Proctor AI as part of the MEST AI Startup Program. I'm open to technical collaborations, AI research partnerships, and opportunities centered around educational infrastructure, automated assessment tools, and AI/hardware co-design.
about.beyond: When I'm not training models or debugging hardware, I train high school students for national and international mathematics and informatics Olympiads. Outside of tech, I spend time exploring classical music (piano, violin composition, and Mozart's Requiem), pencil drawing, and analytic number theory.
